newsitem.title: UK: UK oil stocks up amid Santa Fe North Sea oil deal. [corrected 09:20 gmt]
newsitem.headline: UK oil stocks up amid Santa Fe North Sea oil deal. [corrected 09:20 gmt]

text.p: Shares in British oil companies were higher on Tuesday as Norway's Saga Petroleum was expected to clinch British-based Santa Fe for around $1.2 billion (Corrects from million).
Analysts said the expected price tag was perceived to be high, and the Financial Times newspaper said that Saga could be paying up to a 50 percent premium.
"It is a very high price and the second bidder was not far behind, suggesting Saga is not being stupid," said one trader.
Shares in Enterprise Oil were up 3-1/2p to 596p and Lasmo put on 2p to 221p.
Traders said the deal, which has not yet been confirmed, will provide a boost to the shares of UK exploration companies Lasmo and Enterprise with interests in the North Sea.
Shell Transport and Trading was also 4-1/2p higher at 987-1/2p and British Petroleum was up 5p at 686p.
The FT newspaper added that due to the recent advance in oil shares any positive reaction to the North Sea oil deal would be a good opportunity to take profits.
